Today, October 1, Virgin Islanders honor Contract Day.

After our ancestors took their freedom from chattel slavery in 1848, the Labor Act of 1849 created a new kind of bondage. Workers were bound to one plantation for a full year, with a day wage and restricted movement, able to change estates only on Contract Day. It was freedom in name only.

On October 1, 1878, when rumors of reform proved false, 30 years of frustration ignited the St. Croix Labor Rebellion, known to us as Fireburn. It was led by four women we revere as our Queens: Mary Thomas, Mathilda McBean, Susanna "Bottom Belly" Abrahamson, and Axeline "Queen Agnes" Salomon.

They demanded fair wages and the repeal of the Labor Act, and many paid with their lives. From their sacrifice came reforms that dismantled the labor system.

Today we honor our heritage and remember their courage. 🔥

Congress decides what gets funded, and the President is required to follow those decisions. That is NOT optional. 

And if you don’t believe me, take it from the Government Accountability Office, Congress’s non-partisan watchdog, who thinks it’s illegal too.

My Democrat and Republican colleagues and I on the House Appropriations Committee have spent the last year fighting over, negotiating, and deciding how every single dollar of this funding should be spent.

Trump & his Budget Director Russ Vought are now trying to get around all of that with something called a “pocket rescission.”

Here’s how it’s supposed to work: if the President wants to cancel funding Congress already approved, he sends Congress a request. Congress has 45 days to approve or reject that request. If Congress says no, the President has no choice but to release it. 

Except Trump waited until there were only FIVE DAYS left in the fiscal year.

He is denying Congress the opportunity to even make a decision, and it’s a clear violation of the Constitution.

The President does not get to just cancel $1 billion that Congress passed, and he himself signed into law without consulting Congress.

It’s time to close this loophole once and for all.

U.S. citizen commits suicide after mom detained—blames ICE in his goodbye note.

"To the ICE agent who took away my mom: I hope it was worth it," he wrote.

"I can’t handle any more injustice in this world."

His mom wasn't even person they were after—she didn't even match photo.

Minerva Terrones Dominguez had just gotten off a bus when agents said she "looked like someone" they had a warrant for.

A federal judge later ruled her detention unlawful.

But it was too late—her son was dead.

Samuel Gonzalez Terrones, 21, suffered from mental health issues—and relied on his mom as his main caregiver.

Incident occurred in San Bernardino, California—where the woman had lived for 33 years with no criminal record.

Posting first full length, English translated, and credited video here to help raise awareness.

My statement with @RepMcGovern and @RepGaramendi:  

We are deeply alarmed by increasing violence in Ethiopia, including the Ethiopian military strike last week on an aid convoy delivering assistance in Tigray.

The 2022 Pretoria Agreement that silenced the guns in Northern Ethiopia committed all parties to ceasing hostilities, protecting civilians, allowing humanitarian access to those affected, and undertaking comprehensive transitional justice to hold those responsible for human rights abuses and violations responsible.
